mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 2.5% compresses discount rates and increases equity valuation multiples, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as evidenced by historical correlation between low-rate periods and short-term equity outperformance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 3.0%, it triggers aggressive monetary tightening that increases cost of capital and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in payrolls signals robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE declines and PAYEMS increases.

mechanism_narrative: In expansionary economic regimes, rising housing starts (HOUST) and strong retail sales (RSAFS) signal accelerating consumer demand that increases corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST and RSAFS are rising in expansionary regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts (HOUST) consistently precedes increased consumer spending and economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as a leading indicator of demand expansion.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST rises.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.0%, it indicates labor market weakness that reduces consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in industrial production (INDPRO) and stable inflation (CPIAUCSL <= 255) signals robust supply chain conditions that reduce cost pressures and boost corporate margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO > 109.5 and CPIAUCSL <= 255.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 255), a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive monetary policy that reduces liquidity and equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 255 and FEDFUNDS rises.
